hdr.notGov: A proof of concept · not a Government of India service
hero.sub: Stolen money is split across accounts within minutes. Every other portal spends those minutes on a form. This one asks the banks to hold your money first and collects the details afterwards.
hero.trust2: Banks contacted in under a minute
hero.trust3: Nothing here files a real complaint
tiles.sub: Pick the closest one. You don't need to know what the crime is called, and you will never be asked which district it belongs to.
tiles.t1body: UPI, card, net banking or wallet. We contact the banks before we ask you anything else.
tiles.t2body: Blackmail, intimate images, stalking, or abuse of a child. You can report without giving your name.
tiles.t3body: Impersonation, a hacked account, or a fake profile using your name.
home.victimH2: One report currently freezes every account on the line — including the shopkeeper's.
home.victimBody: He sold a phone and was paid ₹5,000. Three transfers earlier, that money had been stolen. Today his entire balance is frozen with no notice, and getting it back can mean travelling to a police station in another state. It takes months.
home.trailBody: We hold the disputed ₹5,000 and leave the other ₹9,95,000 working. He is told the moment it happens, and can clear it from his phone in about two minutes.
home.stat: Of roughly ₹52,969 crore reported stolen, about 2.18% has reached the people it was taken from. That is the number this rebuild is measured against — not complaints registered.
home.learnSub: Each one is the script as it is actually spoken — how the call opens, the words they use, and the single tell that gives it away.
home.quickCheck: Check a UPI ID before you pay
home.quickVerify: Verify an officer who called you
foot.helpSub: Free, 24×7, in your language. The faster you call, the more can be held.
foot.discStrong: Sahaay is a student proof of concept, not a government service.
foot.discBody: It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to I4C, the Ministry of Home Affairs, or cybercrime.gov.in. No real complaint is filed here and no real data is processed.
foot.realRoute: To report an actual cybercrime in India, call 1930 or use cybercrime.gov.in.
fz.bannerSub: For unauthorised transfers, UPI scams, card fraud and phishing.
fz.time: Time matters. Money reported within 24 hours has by far the highest chance of being held.
fz.noDeadline: There is no deadline. People report weeks later and still get results — this only helps us decide what to do first.
fz.when1sub: Money can often be caught before it moves on again
fz.when2sub: Banks can still place a hold on whatever is left
fz.when3sub: Your report still freezes the account and strengthens every case against them
fz.called: Yes, I have an incident ID
fz.pasteSub: Fastest option — we read every field out of it. Every character works.
fz.mobileSub: We verify this while the freeze is going out — not before. Your money is never waiting on an OTP.
fz.submitBlocked: Enter the amount and bank to continue
fz.nonBank: This was crypto, a gift card, or a closed wallet
fz.nonBankSub: Binance TXID, gift card PIN, Telegram escrow and similar.
fz.noBeneficiary: Don't know who received it? Leave it blank. Your reference is enough to trace where the money landed.
rc.holdingSub: You didn't have to register, pick a category, or choose a district. We started before asking you anything else.
rc.rbi: You reported inside the RBI 3-day window
rc.rbiSub: We've stamped and signed the exact moment you reported. Under RBI rules on unauthorised electronic transactions, that timestamp is your proof of zero liability — keep it.
rc.nothingWaiting: Your case is already open. Details make it stronger, but nothing is waiting on you.
ct.whereis: Here's exactly where your case is
ct.contactNote: They will contact you from a number you can verify on this site. Nobody will ask you for an OTP or a payment.
ct.escalate: Escalate — this deadline is at risk
ct.escalated: Escalated. The missed deadline was attached automatically as evidence — you didn't have to find anyone's phone number.
ln.smallAmount: A small amount of your money is on hold
ln.cardsWork: cards, UPI and transfers all work
ln.notifiedSame: you were notified the same second
ln.currentSystem: On the current system, this would look different
ln.mistakeSub: Show us the payment was legitimate. Takes about two minutes — no branch visit, no travel, no paper.
sc.sub: Check an identifier below, or skip straight to the six signs that need no database at all.
sc.lookup: Check a UPI ID, number or link
sc.demoNote: This prototype searches a small seeded set, not real complaints. On the live system it would query the reports already held by I4C.
sc.doNotPay: Do not pay. Do not share an OTP.
sc.notSafe: Nobody in this demo set has reported it. That is not the same as safe — most frauds are only reported after the money is gone.
sc.useFlags: Check it against the six signs below instead. They are more reliable than any list.
sc.servicesSub: Most people have never heard of them, which is the actual problem. These are live government services and they work right now — this prototype is not a substitute for any of them.
sc.flagsSub: A fraudster can always move to a new UPI ID. They cannot stop needing you to do these things — which makes these more reliable than any database.
sc.nationalH2: You are not the only one this happened to
vo.sub: Every real officer who contacts you about a case gets a code tied to that case. Ask for it. Check it here.
vo.demoCodes: Demo codes: 483921 is real, anything else is not.
vo.neverOtp: Even so: a real officer will never ask you for an OTP, a password, or a payment of any kind.
vo.noOfficer: No officer is contacting you about any case.
vo.noDigitalArrest: Police do not arrest people over a video call. There is no such thing as a digital arrest. You are not in trouble — someone is trying to frighten you into paying.
rp.withoutNameSub: You get a code to track it and add to it later. We never learn who you are, and nobody can ask us.
rp.withDetailsSub: An officer can call you, and you can be told what happened. Needed if you want anything back.
rp.wherePlaceholder: A link, a username, or just the app name
rp.addAnythingSub: In any language. There is no minimum length, and every character works.
rp.startsBefore: We start before asking you anything else.
rp.keepCode: Keep this code somewhere safe. It is the only way back to this report, and it is not linked to you in any way — if you lose it, nobody can recover it for you, which is exactly what makes it anonymous.
rp.officerReach: An officer can reach you about this. You can follow it from your case list at any time.
rp.next1: Platforms have been asked to preserve the records now, before their own retention clock deletes them.
rp.next2: A cyber police station is assigned from where the content is hosted — you were never asked to pick a district.
rp.next3anon: You can add to this report later with your code, without ever giving a name.
rp.next3named: You will be told when it is assigned, and by when.
db.unaffected: of your balance is unaffected and fully usable.
db.nothingFiled: Nothing filed yet. Try the 60-second report — you'll see money held before you've typed anything else.
lg.sub: Tap any card to sign in — no password needed here.
lg.short: Short on time? Start with Suresh.
lg.shortSub: He did nothing wrong and is the person the current system harms invisibly. It's the part of this project you won't have seen elsewhere.
as.title: Sahaay assistant
as.subtitle: Not a real officer. Never asks for an OTP.
as.greeting: Tell me what happened in your own words — in any language. If money has already gone, say so first and I'll get you straight to the fastest thing.
as.emergency: For a real emergency call 1930. This is a student project and files no real complaint.
as.opener1: Someone is calling me about a parcel
st.sub: Written by people who reported, and verified against their own case number. Nobody here is a made-up example.
st.notAllSuccess: These are not all success stories.
st.notAllSuccessSub: Most reported money is never recovered, and pretending otherwise would be its own kind of dishonesty. The accounts that end badly are often the most useful ones to read.
st.writeYoursSub: You can write once your case reaches an outcome. We check it against your case number, so every story here comes from someone who actually went through the process — and you never have to use your real name.
st.lesson: What they want you to know
lc.sub: Not a list of rules. Each one below is the actual script — how the call opens, what they say, and the single thing that gives it away.
lc.everyScam: Every scam, as it actually sounds
lc.askingNow: Someone is asking you for money right now?
hp.sub: Plain answers, most urgent first. If money has just left your account, start with the first section.
hp.happening: If this is happening right now
hp.happeningSub: Report first and read afterwards. Every minute lowers what can be recovered.
rk.harassment.title: Someone is threatening or blackmailing you
rk.harassment.lede: You have not done anything wrong, and you are not in trouble. You can do this without giving your name.
rk.harassment.raceDetail: We ask the platforms to remove it and to preserve the account records before they are deleted on their own schedule.
rk.harassment.s.intimate.label: Private photos or videos of me are being used
rk.harassment.s.intimate.sub: Shared, threatened, or edited from ordinary photos.
rk.harassment.s.intimate.first: Do not pay and do not reply. Screenshot the profile and the demand before you block — evidence disappears the moment they delete the account.
rk.harassment.s.blackmail.label: Someone is demanding money to stay quiet
rk.harassment.s.blackmail.sub: Sextortion, a threatened leak, or a fake recording.
rk.harassment.s.blackmail.first: Paying proves the leverage works and a second demand almost always follows. Stop replying and keep everything they sent you.
rk.harassment.s.stalking.label: Someone will not leave me alone
rk.harassment.s.stalking.sub: Repeated messages, fake accounts, following me between apps.
rk.harassment.s.stalking.first: Keep the messages rather than deleting them. A pattern across weeks is what makes this provable.
rk.harassment.s.child.label: A child is involved
rk.harassment.s.child.sub: Content involving a minor, or a child being contacted.
rk.harassment.s.child.first: This is treated as the highest priority and can be reported entirely anonymously. Do not share or forward the material to anyone, including to show what happened.
rk.harassment.s.other.label: Something else
rk.harassment.s.other.sub: It does not match anything above.
rk.harassment.s.other.first: Describe it in your own words below, in any language. A situation that does not fit the list is not a smaller problem — new methods appear before anyone has a name for them.
rk.harassment.safety.0: You can leave this page instantly with the Quick exit button, or by pressing Escape three times.
rk.harassment.safety.1: Nothing here is stored on this device once you leave.
rk.harassment.safety.2: You never have to give your name for this kind of report.
rk.impersonation.title: Someone is pretending to be you
rk.impersonation.lede: A fake profile, or your name and photos used to cheat other people.
rk.impersonation.raceDetail: We ask the platform to suspend it and to preserve its records, so the people already being contacted stop being deceived.
rk.impersonation.s.profile.label: There is a fake profile using my name or photos
rk.impersonation.s.profile.sub: On social media, a marketplace, or a dating app.
rk.impersonation.s.profile.first: Do not message the account yourself. Screenshot the profile URL and any conversations others have shown you.
rk.impersonation.s.money.label: Someone is asking my contacts for money as me
rk.impersonation.s.money.sub: Friends or family being messaged for an urgent transfer.
rk.impersonation.s.money.first: Tell your contacts directly, on a channel the impersonator does not control. That stops the loss faster than any takedown.
rk.impersonation.s.documents.label: My documents or identity were used
rk.impersonation.s.documents.sub: A SIM, a loan, or an account opened in my name.
rk.impersonation.s.documents.first: Check what is registered against you: TAFCOP shows every SIM in your name, and it is free.
rk.impersonation.s.other.label: Something else
rk.impersonation.s.other.sub: It does not match anything above.
rk.impersonation.s.other.first: Describe it in your own words below, in any language. If you have a link or a username, that is the single most useful thing you can give us.
rk.impersonation.safety.0: Do not confront the account. It tells them to move before the records are preserved.
rk.impersonation.safety.1: Keep the profile link — it is the single most useful thing for a takedown.
rk.account.title: Your account was hacked
rk.account.lede: Email, social media, or banking access taken over.
rk.account.raceDetail: We ask the provider to end every active session and to preserve the login records showing where the access came from.
rk.account.s.email.label: My email was taken over
rk.account.s.email.sub: The one that resets everything else.
rk.account.s.email.first: Start here rather than anywhere else. Email is the master key — whoever holds it can reset every other account you own.
rk.account.s.social.label: My social media account
rk.account.s.social.sub: Posting as me, or messaging my contacts.
rk.account.s.social.first: Warn your contacts on a different channel. The account is being used to reach them, not you.
rk.account.s.banking.label: My banking or payment app
rk.account.s.banking.sub: Transactions I did not make, or a device I do not recognise.
rk.account.s.banking.first: If money has already left, report that first — it is a different and faster path.
rk.account.s.other.label: Something else
rk.account.s.other.sub: It does not match anything above.
rk.account.s.other.first: Describe it in your own words below. If you can still sign in, change the password now from a device you trust.
rk.account.safety.0: Change the password from a different device, not the one that may be compromised.
rk.account.safety.1: Remove any screen-sharing app you were asked to install.
rp.notSureNote: Not sure which one? Pick whichever is closest — nothing is locked in, and the first question on every path is what happened rather than what it is called.
